Real defect introduced by this diff.

judged_text: Salesforce success check uses response.statusText !== 'OK' (salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86) instead of response.ok — the HTTP reason phrase is optional per RFC 7230 and empty on HTTP/2 connections and some proxies, so a successful 200 is misclassified as a failure and throws HttpError 400.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new refresh-token fetch checks success via `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)`. `statusText` is not a reliable indicator of HTTP success (it can be empty or vary), so a successful 2xx response could incorrectly throw, whereas `response.ok`/`response.status` should be used. This is a concrete behavioral defect introduced by the diff.
